title: Top cohomology of algebraic Koszul coefficient reduction
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, r≥0 and f:Fin r→A with span(range f)=I. The explicit reduction morphism c:Hom_A(K_A(f),A)→Hom_A(K_A(f),A/I) [new-j3-koszul-quotient-coefficient-complex] induces an isomorphism on cohomology in degree r. Neither Koszul regularity nor I≠A nor A≠0 is required.

source.place: lemma-regular-immersion-ext, affine dual Koszul coefficient comparison

proof.text: The ordered top wedge spans wedge^r A^r, so top evaluation on the A-dual is injective. The exterior basis shows wedge^(r+1) A^r=0 and makes every Koszul term projective. Therefore postcomposition with the surjective quotient map is surjective in every degree, by projective lifting.

Expand contraction on the ordered top wedge using the Koszul differential formula. It is a sum of complementary wedges with coefficients ±f_j. Pairing with each complementary coordinate functional gives ±f_j. Both signs are units. The incoming image evaluated on the top wedge is precisely I. Injectivity of evaluation identifies the kernel of top coefficient reduction with the incoming image for r>0.

On every wedge the contraction coefficients belong to I. Hence every quotient-valued differential is zero. Apply the short-complex opcycles description of homology: a surjective middle comparison with kernel the incoming image induces a bijection from opcycles to the target middle term.

For r=0, generation forces I=0. The quotient map is injective and top evaluation is injective, so the kernel of top reduction is zero, also the incoming image. The same opcycles proof applies. All formulas hold over the zero ring and for I=A.
